clue.text: Secondary road straight ahead leads to coastal resort

parts.note: a B-road is a secondary road in Britain, abbreviated B
right on is an idiom for straight ahead, keep going forward

explanation.surface: Directions telling a driver to stay on a minor road all the way to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside town on England's south coast; B-roads are Britain's minor routes, below A-roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a well-known seaside town in Sussex, an example of a coastal resort.

clue.text: It's sung to advertise the dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
an ad is the short form of advertisement, the means to advertise

explanation.surface: Something sung as publicity for an upcoming dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song, something that is sung.

clue.text: Part of foot essential for marching properly

explanation.surface: A body part every soldier needs on the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential for' links the two senses while making the surface about drill.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched middle of the foot is one sense; soldiers keeping in step are marching in time together.

clue.text: Aspired to become chief journalist after the spring

indicators.note: after places the editor piece behind the spring piece

parts.note: a hop is a small spring or jump
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor, the chief journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Someone who wished to rise to editor after starting in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season but means a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to want or wish for something, which is what having hoped means.

clue.text: Play part by former pupil is morally offensive

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school
a scene is a division of a play

explanation.surface: An old boy's role in a school play turns out to be indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene describes something indecent and offensive to accepted moral standards.

clue.text: Climbed up in an hierarchical system

explanation.surface: Someone who rose step by step through a rigid ranking structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaled means ascended a height, and also arranged in graded ranks or levels on a scale.

clue.text: Firm gets me a profit in return

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
taken as written
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A company rewarding someone with a profit in exchange for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' looks like a phrase about a deal; the definition is 'return' as in go back to a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To come again is to go back to a place once more, to revisit.

clue.text: Shiny piece of Lulu's trousseau

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something gleaming among the items a bride named Lulu takes into her marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustrous means having a sheen or glow, so it is a synonym of shiny.

clue.text: Stranger described by the German as a feeble creature

indicators.note: described in its sense of drawn around, so the German article encloses the other word

parts.note: der is the German word for the (masculine)
odder means more strange

explanation.surface: A German speaker describes an odd weakling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun but is the comparative adjective ODDER; 'described by' puts it inside DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodderer is a person who totters shakily through age or weakness.

clue.text: Final delivery from the army bugler

parts.note: last means final
the post is the mail delivery

explanation.surface: The last mail round of the day, with a military bugler involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Post is the bugle call played at military funerals and at day's end.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call sounded at military funerals and remembrance ceremonies is something an army bugler plays.

clue.text: First person complaining of exploitation raised a laugh

parts.note: am is the first-person form of the verb to be (I am)
used is how someone complaining of being exploited feels: they say they've been used

explanation.surface: Someone moans about being taken advantage of and, oddly, gets a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Together the pieces read as the complaint 'I am used'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have entertained someone into laughing is to have amused them, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Make time to produce a feature

indicators.note: make in the sense of form something new out of the given letters

explanation.surface: Advice to find a spare hour so as to put together a newspaper feature.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is an article or piece in a newspaper, which is a feature.

clue.text: Ten madmen need correction

indicators.note: the letters of these two words must be corrected into a different order

explanation.surface: Ten lunatics require straightening out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an amendment is a correction, and the letters of TEN MADMEN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to correct or improve a text.

clue.text: Unusually eager to give consent

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the next word are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly keen to say yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to say yes to a proposal, to give consent.

clue.text: Bill takes mining engineer to the summit

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
ME is the abbreviation for mining engineer

explanation.surface: A man named Bill takes an engineer up a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Problem is that it's spoken in anger

explanation.surface: A troublesome matter that comes out in a heated exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross word is an angry word, while the puzzle itself is a problem to solve.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle of interlocking clues is a problem to solve; separated, cross word means a harsh remark made when annoyed.

clue.text: Mother certain to include English in degree

indicators.note: to include tells us the mother word takes the English letter inside it

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A mother confident she can fit English into a university degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degree' suggests a qualification but means extent, as in 'a measure of success'.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is an amount or extent, as in a measure of success, which is a degree.

clue.text: Valued Roman coins presented to Scottish Education Department

parts.note: the as (plural asses) was a bronze coin of ancient Rome
SED is the abbreviation for Scottish Education Department

explanation.surface: Ancient Roman money handed over to a Scottish government body for valuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessed means appraised, having had a price or worth estimated.

clue.text: Father, when upset, has little desire to eat

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word for father is read bottom to top

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
petite means small or little

explanation.surface: An upset father has little interest in his food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PA into AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is hunger, a wish for food.

clue.text: Approve dictum to partake of strong wine

parts.note: sup is to drink or partake of, here as a command, the dictum
port is a strong fortified wine

explanation.surface: Endorsing a saying that recommends drinking fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, 'Sup port!' is the dictum telling you to drink the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To support a plan is to back or endorse it, which is to approve of it.

clue.text: To leave for a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Departing for a West African destination.
explanation.definitionFit: To go means to depart; Togo is a small nation on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Yearn to be evergreen

explanation.surface: A wish to stay forever young.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to long for something; the pine is a coniferous tree that keeps its needles all year.

clue.text: Get professional therapy

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a cure is a remedy or treatment, a therapy

explanation.surface: Advice to seek treatment from an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure is to obtain or acquire something, which is to get it.

clue.text: Aim to express disapproval

explanation.surface: Setting out to voice a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: An object is a goal or purpose; to object is to protest or raise an objection.

clue.text: He declares it of interest to a classical numismatist

definitions.text: it of interest to a classical numismatist

explanation.surface: A man announces something a collector of ancient coins would care about.
explanation.walkthrough: A numismatist collects coins.
explanation.definitionFit: One who states something is a declarer; the stater was also a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Paradoxically they could be the odds

definitions.text: Paradoxically they could be the odds

parts.words: Paradoxically they could be the odds
parts.note: numbers that are not odd can be the betting odds, when a bookmaker offers a one-to-one price

explanation.surface: A contradiction about numbers that are both one thing and its opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, a one-to-one price is called by this name, so the opposite of odd numbers can be the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Even money is a bookmaker's price where the stake is matched, so this term names odds.

clue.text: Quality dress is a practice to encourage

parts.note: good, as in of good quality
a habit is a style of dress, such as a nun's or a riding habit

explanation.surface: Fine clothing recommended as something to aim for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' is a habit, as in a nun's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesome routine worth fostering is a beneficial regular behaviour.

clue.text: Ambassador takes paintings from the centre

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
art covers paintings

explanation.surface: A diplomat removes artworks from a gallery in the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the centre' looks like the source of the paintings but defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or middle of something is called its heart.

clue.text: No American soldier has since returned to Ho Chi Minh City

indicators.note: returned means all the pieces that come before it are read backwards together

parts.note: taken as written
GI is a US soldier
as means since, because

explanation.surface: No American serviceman has gone back to Vietnam's largest city since the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses NOGIAS into the city's former name.
explanation.definitionFit: Saigon was the former name of Vietnam's largest city before 1976.

clue.text: Fashionable fish in the finest capital of Europe

indicators.note: in tells us the fashionable and fish pieces sit inside the word for finest

parts.note: best means finest
U means upper-class, socially acceptable or fashionable
to dap is to fish by letting bait bob on the water surface

explanation.surface: A trendy fish dish served in the best restaurant of a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' is a verb, DAP, not a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary, a European capital.

clue.text: Is terrified of disturbing adders

indicators.note: disturbing says the letters of the snakes are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone frightened of stirring up venomous snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to fear it greatly.

clue.text: One willing to examine a rocky elevation

parts.note: test means examine
a tor is a rocky hill or outcrop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A keen volunteer ready to inspect a rocky hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One willing' suggests eagerness; it is one who makes a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, so one who wills property.
